title: eBay International Shipping replaces the Global Shipping Programme
summary: Eligible sellers are being moved in phases from the Global Shipping Programme to eBay International Shipping. It waives international selling fees and covers returns, loss and damage for items in the UK worth up to £900 outside restricted categories. You can opt out, but you cannot go back to GSP.
note: eBay says it starts in August 2026. Your date depends on when eBay emails you.

title: 1.5% fuel and logistics surcharge added to FBA fees
summary: A 1.5% surcharge now applies to FBA fulfilment fees in the UK. Amazon says it averages about 5p a unit. Multi-Channel Fulfilment picked up the same surcharge from 2 May 2026.
note: Amazon calls it temporary but has not given an end date.

title: Royal Mail annual price change
summary: Stamp, parcel and online postage prices changed. Rebuild your postage costs from the current price guide before you reprice anything.

title: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax starts for income over £50,000
summary: Sole traders and landlords whose self-employment and property income was over £50,000 in 2024 to 2025 must keep digital records and send quarterly updates. The threshold falls to £30,000 from April 2027 and £20,000 from April 2028.

title: eBay agrees to buy Depop
summary: eBay agreed to buy Depop from Etsy. Depop is expected to keep its name and platform. This is a change of owner, not a fee change.
note: The deal was subject to approvals when announced.

title: Business sellers: per-order fee rises to 40p on orders over £10
summary: For UK business sellers the per-order fee on orders over £10 went from 30p to 40p. Final value fees also changed in some categories, including Business, Office and Industrial.

title: Lower referral fees on low-priced items, Low-Price FBA extended to £20
summary: Referral fees fell on lower-priced Home, Pet and Grocery items, and Low-Price FBA rates now cover products priced at £20 or less. The UK deal fee cap was also lowered.
note: First announced for 1 February 2026, then brought forward.

title: FBA parcel fees and clothing referral fees cut
summary: UK FBA fulfilment fees for parcels fell by an average of 26p a unit and Clothing and Accessories referral fees dropped on items up to £20. Some storage, return and liquidation fees went up.

title: Second Class letters move to alternate weekday delivery
summary: Royal Mail can now deliver 2nd Class letters on alternate weekdays, still within three working days, and no longer on Saturdays. 1st Class stays next day, six days a week. Parcels are not affected.

title: DHL eCommerce UK to merge with Evri
summary: Evri announced a merger with DHL eCommerce UK. The DHL premium network becomes Evri Premium. Not a price change.

title: Plan to raise the tax return threshold for trading income to £3,000
summary: The government said it will raise the point at which trading income needs a Self Assessment return from £1,000 to £3,000. No start date has been set, so the £1,000 rule still applies until it is.

title: Buyer Protection changes for private and business sellers
summary: On private sellers' items the buyer pays a Buyer Protection fee shown with the price, and the seller is paid once the item is delivered. Coupons and multi-buy became business-only tools.

title: Returns processing fee for high-return products
summary: Amazon brought in a returns processing fee for products with high return rates, extended the aged inventory surcharge and changed storage fees.

title: First platform reports sent to HMRC
summary: Platforms such as eBay, Vinted, Etsy and Depop sent HMRC details of 2024 sellers with 30 or more sales or about £1,700 or more, and gave those sellers a copy. HMRC confirmed this is not a new tax.

title: Product safety rules (GPSR) for sales into the EU and Northern Ireland
summary: New EU product safety rules apply to products sold into Northern Ireland and the EU, including second-hand goods. They need a responsible person there and safety information on listings. Sales within Great Britain are not covered.

title: Selling becomes free for private sellers in most categories
summary: UK private sellers stopped paying final value fees and the regulatory operating fee, except in motors, property and classifieds. A fee still applies to items sent outside the UK.

title: TikTok Shop UK commission rises to 9%
summary: The commission on completed UK orders went up to 9% including VAT, worked out on the order total including shipping the buyer pays. New sellers can get lower rates for a time.

title: Etsy Creativity Standards
summary: Etsy's rules now sort items into made, designed, handpicked or sourced by the seller, and listings show buyers which one applies. The standards also cover AI-generated art.

title: Depop buyer marketplace fee starts
summary: UK buyers now pay a marketplace fee on each purchase, which pays for Depop removing its seller fee.

title: Free to sell pre-owned clothing for private sellers
summary: UK private sellers stopped paying selling fees on clothing. Replaced by free selling in almost all categories from 30 September 2024.

title: Depop removes the 10% selling fee for UK sellers
summary: New listings from UK sellers paid in pounds no longer pay the 10% selling fee. Payment processing fees still apply.

title: Digital platform reporting rules come into force
summary: UK platforms must collect seller details and report sellers with 30 or more sales, or about £1,700 or more, in a calendar year to HMRC.
